create.name: Gary Gach
create.bio:
Gary Gach is a San Francisco writer and Zen practitioner whose main teacher is the Vietnamese monk Thich Nhat Hanh, in whose core community he has been ordained. His path into meditation started early: a Quaker retreat in 1964, an introduction to Zen from Paul Reps, and zazen training in San Francisco under Dainin Katagiri Roshi, with encounters along the way with Alan Watts and Shunryu Suzuki Roshi.

He is best known for The Complete Idiot's Guide to Buddhism, which he organised as two halves, first the Buddha, his teaching and the community, then how the path plays out in relationships, work, food and culture. His later book, Pause … Breathe … Smile, treats those three words as a whole practice: pausing to set an intention, breathing to bring body and mind together, and smiling as a doorway to wisdom. Gach is also a poet and translator, has compiled a collection of Buddhist poems from the Beats to hip-hop, and has rendered the Persian poet Hafez into English. For many years he has hosted a small weekly mindfulness group in the Plum Village style, with sitting, walking and sharing, and he leads mindfulness sessions at conferences and gatherings.
